subject: SpaceX catches Ship 42 🦾, thousands petition for Jensen ✍️, Tesla opens Cybercab orders 🚕
notes: No funding rounds, acquisitions, IPOs, funds or AI model pricing in this issue; top news stories only. The FAA network outage quick link was left out to stay within the eight-story limit.

stories.headline: SpaceX catches Ship 42 on Flight 15, the first upper-stage catch; Booster 22 aborts its catch and splashes down in the Gulf
stories.quote: After 14 orbits, Ship 42 made a 10-second single-engine deorbit burn and was caught by the tower's chopsticks 22.5 hours after launch, the first upper-stage catch.

facts.text: Ship 42 deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and had its heat shield checked using satellite cameras.
facts.quote: It deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and had its heat shield checked using satellite cameras.

facts.text: The V3 booster's boostback ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm and it diverted to a Gulf splashdown; root cause under investigation.
facts.quote: The V3 booster's boostback ended early on a low-fuel-mass alarm, so guidance detected it was off-position and diverted to a Gulf splashdown, with the root cause still under investigation.

stories.headline: Petition backed by Musk, Masad and Sweeney asks Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang during the investigation; Huang resigned Thursday, CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO
stories.quote: Huang resigned Thursday after admitting a relationship with an executive US intelligence suspects of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Nvidia fell 2% on Friday.

facts.text: The petition says it has over 115,000 signatures, including 5,965 current Nvidia employees and 63,063 shareholders.
facts.quote: The petition says it has over 115,000 signatures, including 5,965 current Nvidia employees and 63,063 shareholders, and argues Huang was removed without due process

facts.text: Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting a relationship with an executive US intelligence suspects of spying for China.
facts.quote: Huang resigned Thursday after admitting a relationship with an executive US intelligence suspects of spying for China.

facts.text: CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
facts.quote: CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.

stories.headline: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders to select customers at $29,990 plus $299 per month, limited to Robotaxi geofences
stories.quote: Tesla says the Cybercab will run unsupervised only inside the same geofences as its Robotaxi service, with delivery limited to a handful of Texas cities and an estimated date of December.

facts.text: Pre-order price is $29,990 plus $299 per month, for select customers.
facts.quote: TESLA OPENS CYBERCAB PRE-ORDERS TO SELECT CUSTOMERS AT $29,990 PLUS $299 PER MONTH, GEOFENCED TO ROBOTAXI'S AREAS

facts.text: Musk called the $299 monthly fee too high and said nationwide availability depends on regulatory approval.
facts.quote: Musk called the $299 monthly fee too high, saying it should match the roughly $115 per month for FSD and connectivity, and that nationwide availability depends on regulatory approval.

stories.headline: Researchers say starting-weight layouts show Chinese AI models including DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3 and Ling-3.1-flash were trained on Nvidia Blackwell chips
stories.quote: DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1-flash matched Blackwell, while earlier models matched Hopper.

facts.text: The headline says six Chinese models were shown to have trained on Blackwell; the text names four.
facts.quote: RESEARCHERS MATCHED THE RANDOM STARTING WEIGHTS OF CHINESE AI MODELS TO GPU THREAD LAYOUTS TO SHOW SIX TRAINED ON BLACKWELL

facts.text: Method: PyTorch seeds weights across 2,048 threads per SM, and SM counts differ by chip (132 Hopper, 148 B200/B300, 152 GB200/GB300).
facts.quote: PyTorch seeds a model's weights with random numbers split across 2,048 threads per SM, so each chip lays them out differently: 132 SMs for Hopper, 148 for B200/B300, 152 for GB200/GB300.

stories.headline: ULA's Vulcan loses 40 Amazon Leo satellites about 10 minutes into flight; Centaur's burn is the suspect
stories.quote: This was ULA's first total failure since 2006 and the first Vulcan flight in nine months after its solid booster nozzle fixes.
stories.description: Launch provider operating the Vulcan rocket

facts.text: 40 Amazon Leo satellites were lost about 10 minutes in, with Centaur's burn the suspect.
facts.quote: ULA'S VULCAN LOSES 40 AMAZON LEO SATELLITES ABOUT 10 MINUTES IN, WITH CENTAUR'S BURN THE SUSPECT

facts.text: The BE-4 engines had been retrofitted for the oxygen valve issue behind New Glenn's May pad explosion.
facts.quote: The BE-4s had been retrofitted for the oxygen valve issue behind New Glenn's May pad explosion.

stories.headline: OpenAI folds its standalone robotics team into its main research and Applied organisations
stories.quote: OpenAI moved its robotics researchers into its main research org and its applied robotics and hardware teams into Applied, betting general models can control robots without specialized “robot brains.”

facts.text: OpenAI still plans its own humanoid, with a demo targeted for 2027.
facts.quote: OpenAI still plans its own humanoid, with a demo targeted for 2027, while robotics startups argue real-world deployment data remains their edge.

stories.headline: Applied Materials' total revenue rises 53% to $10.41 billion; semiconductor systems revenue up 64% to $7.99 billion
stories.quote: Total revenue rose 53% to $10.41 billion, with the semiconductor systems unit up from $4.88 billion to $7.99 billion.
stories.description: Supplier of semiconductor manufacturing systems to chipmakers

facts.text: Systems revenue jumped 64% to $7.99B as chipmakers expand fabs; the headline also cites a $5B EPIC Center for shared R&D.
facts.quote: APPLIED MATERIALS' SYSTEMS REVENUE JUMPS 64% TO $7.99B AS CHIPMAKERS EXPAND FABS, WITH A $5B EPIC CENTER FOR SHARED R&D

stories.headline: Federal judge denies Samsung, SK hynix and Micron's motion to dismiss the DRAM price-fixing suit
stories.quote: A federal judge denied Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron's motion to dismiss in full, finding a plausible claim that they restricted conventional DRAM supply and drove prices up 697% over 18 months.
stories.description: DRAM chipmakers named as defendants in a price-fixing suit

facts.text: The judge called the chipmakers' alleged behaviour "hawks flying in formation".
facts.quote: JUDGE KEEPS DRAM PRICE-FIXING SUIT ALIVE, CALLING THE CHIPMAKERS' ALLEGED BEHAVIOR “HAWKS FLYING IN FORMATION”
